headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Goose can write/modify the workspace while Superset may consume shared outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP; its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress, so if it ingests Goose-produced files or dashboard inputs, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workspace setups, though not proven.
conditions: IF Goose writes instructions or data files into a workspace that Superset later reads
IF Superset parses Goose-generated content as trusted configuration or query input
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of Goose-written files by Superset
Require manual review of any shared artifacts before import
Use read-only mounts for Superset where feasible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, handles model-provider keys and extension tokens, and has broad network egress. Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. If both operate on the same workspace, Goose can expose file contents to its backend or extensions while Superset can surface those artifacts, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets or sensitive source code
IF Goose sends workspace content to configured model providers or MCP extensions
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared cwd
Use separate service accounts and credentials
Restrict Goose to non-sensitive directories
Audit which files Superset can read from shared storage
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and subprocess capability; its shared-state model is via filesystem. Superset can access APIs and network egress. If both touch the same mutable workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git changes can collide, and the rubric treats overlapping write capability on shared mutable resources as high risk.
conditions: IF Goose and Superset operate on the same repository or writable directory
IF Superset writes or mutates shared artifacts through its API-backed workflows
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git mutation in Goose for shared repos
Run Superset read-only against shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, shell commands, and filesystem changes; Superset can consume API-driven inputs and present analytics outputs. If Superset treats Goose-produced artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from generated content into downstream reports or actions. The pair is not documented as having verification gates, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Superset imports Goose-generated files or queries without validation
IF Goose outputs are used as source-of-truth for dashboards or operational decisions
mitigations: Require human review before import
Add schema validation on Goose outputs
Compare outputs against an independent source
Mark Goose artifacts as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: implement verification checkpoints

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and can move source code/files in cwd over broad egress, while Superset is only documented with allowlisted egress and no sensitive data classes. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced here, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive code or secrets in shared files.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed in the shared workspace
IF Superset is configured to process those files across a jurisdictional boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use separate retention policies for each agent
Restrict Goose to non-regulated projects
Review logging settings for both systems
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
